templates.title: UniFi Controller
templates.description: Ubiquiti UniFi Network Management Controller for managing UniFi devices. Uses qnet network with fixed MAC and MongoDB 7.0.

templates.note:
UniFi Controller web interface at https://localhost:8443.

This stack uses qnet-static-bond0-0094fd with a fixed MAC (02:00:00:00:00:02) and MongoDB 4.4.

⚠️ This is a fresh install — no migration from old UniFi versions. Set up the controller from the setup wizard on first access.

Safe upgrades & rollback
A one-shot unifi-backup container runs before the controller on every deploy. It compares the current controller image tag against the last backed-up version:
  • Upgrade (new tag): automatically creates a mongodump + config archive.
  • Downgrade (revert to a previously deployed tag): automatically restores the matching backup.
  • No change: skips instantly.
The last 7 backups are kept by default.

Manual rollback (if auto-restore is not desired):
  1. Stop the stack in Portainer.
  2. Identify the backup timestamp folder from before the upgrade.
  3. Restore MongoDB: docker run --rm -v /backup/path:/backups mongo:4.4 mongorestore --drop --host=unifi-db -u unifi -p <pass> --authenticationDatabase=admin /backups/<timestamp>/mongo
  4. Extract the config archive: tar xzf /backup/path/<timestamp>/unifi-config.tar.gz -C /config/path
  5. Edit the docker-compose.yml image tag back to the previous version, commit, and redeploy via GitOps.

templates.title: Plex Media Server
templates.description: Plex Media Server: stream your media library to any device. Uses the qnet network with a fixed MAC address.

env.name: TZ
env.label: Timezone
env.description: Timezone for the container (e.g. Europe/Madrid)

env.name: PUID
env.label: User ID (PUID)
env.description: User ID that Plex will run as

env.name: PGID
env.label: Group ID (PGID)
env.description: Group ID that Plex will run as

env.name: PLEX_CLAIM
env.label: Plex Claim Token
env.description: Get your claim token from https://plex.tv/claim (required on first run)

env.name: ADVERTISE_IP
env.label: Advertise IP
env.description: IP or DNS advertised for remote access (e.g. http://plex.calavia.org:32400)

env.name: PLEX_CONFIG_PATH
env.label: Plex config path
env.description: Path where Plex configuration will be stored on the NAS

env.name: PLEX_TRANSCODE_PATH
env.label: Plex transcode path
env.description: Path for Plex transcoding temporary files on the NAS

env.name: PLEX_CPU_LIMIT
env.label: CPU limit (cores)
env.description: Maximum number of CPU cores Plex can use

env.name: PLEX_MEM_LIMIT
env.label: Memory limit
env.description: Maximum memory Plex can use (e.g. 8G, 4096M)

env.name: MEDIA_PATH
env.label: Media path
env.description: Path to your media folder on the NAS

templates.note:
Plex Media Server web interface at http://localhost:32400/web.

This stack uses the qnet-static-bond0-0094fd network with a fixed MAC address (02:00:00:00:00:01) so Plex does not generate a new identity on each restart.

First run: Get a claim token at https://plex.tv/claim and set it in the environment variable PLEX_CLAIM.

Hardware transcoding via /dev/dri is enabled if available on your NAS (Intel Quick Sync).

To add more media paths, go to Volumes in the advanced deployment view and add additional bind mounts.
